base_override.reason: The engine's normalized conservative base ($0.04/sh, median of last 3 FY) and the latest FY (-$0.40/sh) and TTM (-$0.71/sh, ttm.py) all charge the full growth-capex supercycle as if it were maintenance: FY2025 capex $292.6M and TTM capex $338.0M vs D&A of $110.3M / $116.1M, under a disclosed $1.2B 2025-2029 capacity program (plus $400M added 2026-10-12) for AI data-center demand. Charging expansion capex against current earnings power understates the base to ~zero and makes every downstream figure meaningless; the engine's own maintenance definition (capex capped at D&A) is the economically right base, normalized the same way the engine normalizes the conservative one (3-yr median). Construction uses only figures printed in this run's financials_history.csv. Even on this friendlier base the weighted IV@15% ($5.65) sits 94.0% below the $93.88 price — the override does not create the tier, it only makes the shortfall measurable.
base_override.source: Median of the last three fiscal years' maintenance owner's earnings per share from this run's financials_history.csv (oe_maintenance = NI + D&A - min(capex, D&A) - deltaNWC, engine definition): period 2024-01-01 $34,769,000 / 102,744,000 sh = $0.3384; period 2024-12-30 $38,036,000 / 104,098,000 sh = $0.3654; period 2025-12-29 $79,231,000 / 105,453,000 sh = $0.7513; median $0.3654.

moat_against: Filed ROIC proxy was 1.2-5.3% in six of the last nine years — through-cycle returns at or below the cost of capital
PCB fabrication is capital-intensive and contestable: Asian competitors (and customer in-sourcing) can add the same capacity; the current edge is timing, not structure

Demand concentration in the hyperscaler AI capex cycle — the same cycle now driving a $1.2B 2025-29 capex program plus a further $400M announced 2026-10-12; if AI spend digests, the new capacity is stranded cost
New capacity concentrated in China and Penang, Malaysia — tariff, export-control and geopolitical exposure
SBC rising fast ($22.9M FY2024-label to $41.7M FY2025 to $61.3M TTM) and share count creeping up (~0.5%/yr) — owners fund part of the growth story
moat_for: Advanced N+M asymmetrical PCB technology for AI data centers — one of few scaled suppliers, capacity being added brownfield at speed
Aerospace & defense franchise: mission systems, RF/microwave assemblies, $1.7B defense backlog and long program qualifications that are sticky once designed in
Scale: one of the world's largest PCB manufacturers, ~80% of sales tied to AI and defense megatrends per management
Mix shift is lifting filed gross margin (16.5-18.5% FY2022-24 to 20.7% FY2025, 21.2% TTM) and ROIC proxy to 10.3% in FY2025
moat_justification: Weak moat: a cyclical PCB/RF manufacturer whose filed ROIC proxy ran 1.2-5.3% in six of the last nine fiscal years (only FY2018 12.0% and FY2025 10.3% above high-single digits) and whose gross margin lived at 16-19.5% for a decade before the AI mix shift lifted it to 20.7% (FY2025) / 21.2% (TTM). Current strength is a technology-and-capacity position in advanced N+M asymmetrical PCBs plus long defense qualifications — real, but contestable by Asian PCB rivals and hostage to the hyperscaler capex cycle; no network effects, no owned demand, limited pricing power through a cycle.
name: TTM Technologies, Inc.
one_liner: Real AI/defense growth story with a weak moat (3/10) and a capex supercycle that swallows owner's earnings — even on a maintenance-capex base and guided growth it does not clear 15% at $93.88 (weighted IRR 3.36%, weighted IV@15% $5.65; clears 15% only below ~$5.65); the price capitalizes the bull case and then some, it does not discount it.
sector: Electronic Manufacturing / Advanced PCBs & RF Components
